scenes.headline: How FAST-LIO2 fuses LiDAR and an IMU
scenes.sub: One iterated Kalman filter, deskewed scans, point-to-plane matching and a growing map.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Laurel! FAST-LIO2 tracks a moving sensor from LiDAR and an IMU, a hundred times a second on a laptop. Here's the loop inside.

scenes.text: Let the IMU predict, deskew each LiDAR scan, and correct the pose by landing raw points on local planes, iterating one Kalman filter until it settles.
scenes.mark: landing raw points on local planes

steps.say: Between scans, the IMU drives the state forward: position, attitude, velocity, biases and gravity.
A scan takes about a tenth of a second while the sensor moves. Cached IMU poses carry every point to the scan-end frame.

steps.note: repeat until the correction is tiny
steps.say: Each point finds its five nearest map points and fits a plane. The filter pulls points onto their planes, re-matching until the correction is tiny.
The settled state is the odometry, and the scan joins an incremental k-d tree map that updates in place instead of being rebuilt.

scenes.title: The gain that makes it fast
scenes.say: What makes it fast is the Kalman gain. The textbook form inverts a matrix as wide as the number of points: thousands.

parts.note: thousands of point rows, folded into a small block
parts.say: Rewritten, every point's row folds into one small block.

parts.note: one 23 x 23 inverse: the size of the state
parts.say: So the inverse is twenty-three by twenty-three, the size of the state, however many points there are.

scenes.label: from its start after 38 m of path, in the author's Python rebuild
scenes.note: a real Livox bag, one file of about 390 lines
scenes.say: The author's Python rebuild tracked a real sensor recording, returning within about point six metres of its start after thirty-eight metres of path.

scenes.text: FAST-LIO2 is one iterated Kalman filter, with a gain rewritten so thousands of points cost the same as a few.

recap: The IMU predicts; each scan is deskewed
Raw points land on planes, iterated to convergence
A 23 x 23 gain and an incremental map
scenes.say: To recap: predict with the IMU, deskew, land points on planes, and a gain the size of the state.
